topic.title: Michael Jordan bought the Charlotte team for about $275M and sold at a $3B value while it barely won: owners grow with the league, not the scoreboard

title: Michael Jordan paid $275M for a team that barely won. Then what? 🏀
description:
Michael Jordan paid $275M for a basketball team that barely won. So what was it worth when he sold?
Sources: AP, CBS Sports (Aug 2023). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Winning games or owning the team: which made Jordan richer? Comment

lines.text: Michael Jordan paid about $275M for a losing team.
So what was it worth when he finally sold?
On the court, it kept losing. Not one playoff round won while he ran it.
But every NBA team gets an equal share of the league's TV money, win or lose.
And while he owned it, those TV deals got far bigger.
So the team's price climbed with the league, not with the scoreboard.
When he sold, the team was valued at about $3B. That's 10.9× what he paid.
Winning games or owning the team: which made Michael Jordan richer?

'Not one playoff round won' matches both (no playoff series won in 13 seasons). Equal national-TV share is general NBA mechanics (ESPN, SBJ); 2016 deal $24B/9y far bigger than prior. Payoff says 'the team was valued at', true to the majority-stake sale. Description ends with the disclaimer; no advice or imperative.
